rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance (Just Cause Eviction)
rules.requirement: Landlords must have a legally recognized 'just cause' (at-fault or no-fault) to terminate a residential tenancy, must provide specific notices to the tenant and, in some cases, the Commission, and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault terminations.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental properties within the City of San Diego as defined by the ordinance.
rules.penalty: Landlord liable in civil action for wrongful eviction for damages of at least 3x actual economic damages; if relocation assistance not provided, liable for at least 3x required relocation assistance plus actual economic damages; reasonable attorney's fees and costs.
rules.quoted_span: The purpose of the Ordinance is to require Just Cause for termination of residential tenancies consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2, to limit the reasons for termination of a residential tenancy, to require greater tenant relocation assistance in specified circumstances and to provide additional tenant protections.
